newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Gul Technologies sees 15 pct growth 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Gul Technologies sees 15 pct growth 1997.

text.p: Printed circuit board (PCB) maker Gul Technologies Singapore Ltd said on Monday it expected increasing use of micro-electronics in consumer products to spur rapid profit growth over the next few years.

Gul, which announced the terms of its initial public offer (IPO) in Singapore on Monday, is one of Singapore's fastest growing suppliers of PCBs, which are at the heart of electronic devices such as computers and mobile telephones.

Gul president and chief executive officer Jerry Rodrigues told Reuters the company was expanding production to meet demand for the miniature circuits in a range of new products which had previously had few electronic components.
"Over the years, the semi-conductor will control more and more areas of activity," Rodrigues said in an interview.
He said one of the fastest expanding consumers of PCBs was the automotive industry, where computers and electronic circuits where taking over from purely mechanical devices.

"Now you have micro-electronics in engine controls, anti-lock braking systems and they are looking at environmental controls, exhaust systems, fuel injection systems and even comfort controls," he said.
About half Gul's Singapore $117.65 million (US$82.27 million) turnover in 1996 came from sales to computer and electronics giants such as U.S. firm Seagate, he said.
Roughly 20 percent of the company's sales went to the telecommunications industry, around 25 percent to car-makers and five percent for use in medical equipment.
These areas would account for most future growth, he said.
A Gul statement said the firm made a net profit of S$10.38 million in 1996, up 18 percent from S$8.8 million in 1995.
Gul's chief financial officer Ng Hin Lee said the firm ought to be able to maintain growth at around 15 percent in 1997.

"I believe with the track record that we have, and the plan that we have, I think that would be sustainable," Ng told Reuters. He earlier told a news conference the company could "maintain double-digit growth" for the next few years.
Rodrigues said Gul, majority-owned by Singapore main board-listed Tuan Sing Holdings Ltd, was considering opening new factories in either Indonesia or China to take advantage of cheaper labour costs.
He said the company hoped to open its first overseas facility within two years.

Gul is offering 40.2 million new ordinary shares, to be listed on Singapore's second board SESDAQ, at SS$0.58 each. Of the total, 30.15 million shares are offered to the public and 10.05 million sold as placement shares.
Richard Tan, vice president of Overseas Union Bank, which is managing and lead underwriting the share issue, said demand for Gul's placement shares had been "overwhelming".
He said the offer price, which represented a historical price earnings ratio of 12.6 times, was "extremely undemanding".
The issue is expected to raise net proceeds of S$22 million to be used to purchase machinery and equipment, expand production, repay term loans and as additional working capital.
The shares will trade on a when-issued basis from March 17.
